explanation: Genesis never names the fruit. The apple may owe its role to a Latin pun, since malum can mean 'evil' or 'apple'. Some Jewish traditions suggest a fig, grapes or wheat.

claims.text: In Western art and tradition, the forbidden fruit of the Garden of Eden is usually shown as an apple.
The forbidden fruit is not traditionally pictured as an orange, a pear or a peach.
The Book of Genesis does not name the fruit of the tree of knowledge.
Latin malum can mean 'evil' or 'apple', a pun that may have helped make the apple the forbidden fruit.
Some Jewish traditions identify the forbidden fruit as a fig, grapes or wheat.
